# Global agent instructions

This toolkit shares instructions, skills, and plugins across agent CLIs.

## Every task

- Use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
- Read applicable `CONTEXT.md` files. Use their ubiquitous language.
- Before each reply, apply [English coaching](~/.claude/agent-rules/english.md) to the user's message.
- Use bullets only for lists, checklists, or comparisons.
- In Chinese prose, use full-width punctuation and 「」 quotation marks. Do not use `/` as a conjunction.
- When I must run a command that has more than one line or is too long to read easily, write it to a script file. Then give me one short command that runs the script.
- When a step does not need my input, continue. Put status notes in the same message as the next action. Stop and ask only when you cannot continue without me, or before a destructive action.
- Before you report a task that edited files as complete, review your diff. Mark each statement that you could not confirm, and say where you looked.

## Topic rules

Read each matching file before the action. For generated Codex instructions, use the inline section instead.

- [Tools](~/.claude/agent-rules/tooling.md): before searching code, editing files, delegating work, or using tools.
- [Shell](~/.claude/agent-rules/shell.md): before zsh loops, variables, or functions, `ssh` commands, `curl` TLS tests, or `stat`, and after a hook blocks a command.
- [Web](~/.claude/agent-rules/web.md): before web research or reading a web page.
- [Git](~/.claude/agent-rules/git.md): before Git operations, repository moves, file deletion, publishing, or releases.
- [GitHub](~/.claude/agent-rules/github.md): before GitHub, CI, shipping, release, or changelog work.
- [Secrets](~/.claude/agent-rules/secrets.md): before handling secrets, tokens, API keys, or environment variables.
- [Artifacts](~/.claude/agent-rules/artifacts.md): before writing or editing files, commit messages, or generated artifacts.

# Artifact privacy and paths

- Do not include personal identifiers: local account names, home directory names, real names, or email addresses. This rule includes contributor-credit trailers.
- Use `~` for the user's home directory in prose. In code, derive paths from the repository root, `$HOME`, or the script's location.
- Apply these rules to files, commit messages, and generated artifacts, including documentation, comments, and tests.
- The privacy guard (ADR-0011 in agent-scripts) blocks a commit that adds a home path, an email address, or a secret. If it blocks a commit, fix the line or ask the user. Never bypass it.

# English coaching

The user is learning natural English for international work.

- Correct only real grammar or phrasing mistakes in the user's English.
- Do not correct Chinese-only messages, URLs, commands, code, logs, names, quotes, or natural English.
- Be patient and encouraging. Give priority to important mistakes.
- Append corrections at the end of the reply. Use two lines per issue, without quotes or explanations:

  😇 original
  👉 correction (Pattern name)

Patterns: Missing article, Wrong article, Redundant preposition, Gerund vs. base verb, Wrong verb form, Passive voice error, Subject-verb agreement, Double subject, Tense error, Unnatural phrasing, Over-hedging.

Example:

😇 discuss about
👉 discuss (Redundant preposition)

# Git

## Authorization

- Task completion does not authorize commits, pushes, tags, or publication. Leave changes uncommitted unless the user authorizes these actions.
- Push only when the user asks in this task or invokes a workflow that explicitly pushes.
- This rule applies to every repository. Repository rules can define push steps, but cannot authorize a push.
- Rewrite published history only when the user explicitly requests that specific rewrite.
- This includes force-push, rebase onto a pushed base, `filter-branch`, and `filter-repo`.
- `filter-repo` removes `origin` and its remote-tracking refs. Add `origin` again and run `git fetch origin` before `--force-with-lease`, or the lease has nothing to compare.
- `git grep` exits 1 when it finds no match. Under `set -e`, guard it: `git grep ... || true`.
- `reset --hard`, `clean`, and `restore` each require an explicit user request every time.
- Delete files only within the task scope. Never delete or overwrite unknown or unrelated user data.

## Where to work

- Inside a repository, work there. Create a sibling checkout or worktree only when asked.
- Outside a repository, choose a suitable folder. State its path before editing. You may create a worktree without asking.
- Checkouts under `~/Projects` belong to the user. Do not use them as temporary storage.
- Continue if unrelated changes do not overlap your task. Change only your own files.
- Stop and ask if changes overlap, the branch is wrong, or a repository move is unclear.

## Branches

- Change branches only with user consent or permission from a user-invoked workflow.
- `land` and `ship` authorize the branch changes and pushes that they require.
- Finish in the checkout and branch the user expects.

## Commits

- Use Conventional Commits: `feat|fix|refactor|build|ci|chore|docs|style|perf|test`.
- Amend only when asked.
- Keep edits small and easy to review. Do not run repository-wide search-and-replace scripts.
- Apply [artifact privacy](~/.claude/rules/artifacts.md).

# GitHub, CI, and shipping

## GitHub commands

- Use `gh` for GitHub facts. Do not use web search for pull request or issue references.
- Use `--json <fields>` for every `gh` read. Exception: `gh pr diff` has no JSON output.
- The shared cache handles machine-readable output.
- Human-format `gh pr view/list/checks` and `gh run list` bypass the cache. So does bare `gh api graphql`.
- GraphQL and core requests use the personal token.
- `gh api --paginate` bypasses the cache and uses the real token. Use it only when you need the full list.
- For personal repositories, push and write with the repository owner's account. Check the active account before writing.

## Pull requests

- For a pasted GitHub issue or PR URL, first run `git status -sb`.
- If the tree is dirty, report this before making changes. A URL alone does not authorize a push or pull.
- Prefer a fix or rewrite PR, then merge it. Do not close the PR and commit a duplicate directly.
- Review and improve generated code before merging it. Rewrite it fully if this makes it simpler.
- `rewrite commits + land`: simplify the commit stack. Keep only the agreed focused proof. Force-push, then merge.
- For that workflow, refine PR-body proof or monitor CI only when asked.
- After `land`, check out `main`. Run `git pull --ff-only`, then `git status -sb`. Report the result.

## Issues and CI

- If an issue is fixed on `main` with proof, comment with the proof and commit or PR. Then close it.
- `fix ci` authorizes pull, commit, and push. Use `gh run list/view --json ...`.
- Fix and rerun until CI passes. Increase the wait between status checks.

## Shipping and releases

- Only the user can start `ship`, by asking in the current task. Task completion does not authorize shipping.
- `ship` means: update the changelog, make grouped commits, push, then pull. Report "shipped" only after the push to GitHub.
- Publish a version or artifact only after an explicit `release` or `publish` request. A tag or push is not a release.
- Before finishing a release, check that the docs and notes contain the current changelog. Fix missing or stale content.
- Match the existing changelog style. Prefer one-line bullets. Do not wrap prose manually. Thank `@login` for user-visible work by other people. Do not thank the repository owner for their own changes.

# Secrets and environment variables

- Never reveal secret values, including internal secrets. Redact them from output.
- Use the configured secret-management tool. If no tool is identified, ask before retrieving a secret.
- Query only the exact environment variable needed for the task.
- Never run `env`, `set`, `export -p`, or broad secret searches that expose values in a normal shell.
- To store a secret the user gives, tell them to copy it, then run `<cmd> "$(pbpaste | tr -d '\n')" && pbcopy < /dev/null`. A `!` command gets no stdin, so an interactive prompt stores an empty value. Then check the stored length with `wc -c`. Do not print the value.
- After handling a secret or environment variable, remove token variables from each public `gh` write. Use `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_TOKEN -u HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN gh ...`.

# Shell limits and hook details

## zsh

- Never name a variable `status`.
- Use an array for a loop over multiple items. A scalar string does not split into words as in bash.
- Store a command in a function, not a variable: `g() { env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh "$@"; }`. A variable such as `G="env -u X gh"` does not split into words, so `$G args` fails with `command not found`. Give the function a name that is not an alias in the user's profile: `G() { … }` fails with `defining function based on alias`. Check with `type <name>` first.
- `$EPOCHSECONDS` is empty until `zmodload zsh/datetime`. Use `date +%s` instead.
- Quote every URL or path that contains `?`, such as `gh api 'repos/o/r/contents/f?ref=main'`.

## Tools

- A multi-line `sd -F` can match nothing and still exit 0. A hook blocks a newline inside a quoted `sd` pattern.
- For a `sd` pattern that starts with `-`, put `--` before the pattern: `sd -F -- '-L lisp' '-L user-lisp' file`.
- macOS `/usr/bin/curl` (SecureTransport) has no `--tlsv1.3` and exits 4, so a loop over it reports every host as failed. Test TLS 1.3 with `openssl s_client -tls1_3`, or Python `ssl`. Count the failure types before you trust a result of zero passes.
- `stat` is GNU coreutils here: use `stat -c %y file` for the modification time. `stat -f` prints file system status, not file data.

## ssh

- Over `ssh`, the hook does not check the remote command. If the remote host lacks `rg`, `fd`, `sd`, or `eza`, use `grep`, `find`, `sed`, and `ls` there.
- Write a remote script that uses `grep` or `find` to a file with the file tool, then run `ssh host sh -s < file`. The hook reads these words inside a heredoc body as commands and blocks the whole command.

## Hook details

- The modern-CLI hook blocks `grep` at the start of each command segment (after `;`, `&&`, `||`, or a newline). `grep` after `|` stays allowed. It rewrites a simple `find -name`, `sed -i`, or `ls` (flags `l a A 1 h` and one path) to `fd`, `sd`, or `eza`. Any other `ls` runs as typed. Use a classic tool only when the modern tool cannot do the task safely or exactly.
- The Git-read hook blocks `git status`, `log`, `diff`, `rev-parse`, bare `branch`, and `worktree list` when the command does only Git reads (with `cd` and read-only filters such as `| head` or `| rg`). In a chain that also does other work, such as commit, push, then check, the reads run. Global options such as `-C <path>` or `--no-pager` do not change this.
- The curl hook blocks a URL plus only `-s`, `-S`, `-L`, `-f`, and for HEAD a separate `-I`. Any other curl option, such as `-H`, `-m`, `-o`, or `-w`, keeps curl.

## Anvil org module

Anvil's `org` module is off: `my/anvil-modules` in `~/.emacs.d/user-lisp/init-local-anvil.el` leaves it out. It conflicted with interactive Emacs buffers and caused many Syncthing conflict files.

# Tools and task routing

## Find code

1. If the repository has `.codegraph/`, use CodeGraph (`codegraph_explore` or `codegraph explore "<symbols or question>"`) before other code searches or reads. Without `.codegraph/`, skip it. Only the user decides whether to index a repository.
2. Otherwise, locate files with `rg` and `fd`, then read the files found.

## Commands

- Use `rg`, `fd`, `sd`, and `eza`, not `grep`, `find`, `sed -i`, or `ls`. Hooks block or rewrite the classic tools. A blocked command does not run at all, including its other segments: fix it, then run the full command again. Details: [shell.md](~/.claude/agent-rules/shell.md).
- Use `sd` only for one-line patterns. For multi-line replacements, use `Edit` or `file-replace-string`.
- Delete files with `trash <path>`. `rm`, `mv`, and `cp` are interactive aliases (`rm -i`, `mv -i`, `cp -av`) and hang when the target exists. To replace a file, use the Write tool or `cat new > target`.

## Git state and HTTP

When Anvil is reachable, a hook blocks commands that only read Git state, and plain `curl` GET or HEAD requests.

- Read Git state with the `mcp__anvil-emacs-eval__` tools (not `mcp__anvil__`): `git-status`, `git-log`, `git-diff-names` or `git-diff-stats`, `git-head-sha`, `git-branch-current`, and `git-worktree-list`. Use one call for each read. `git diff -- <path>` and `git diff --check` stay allowed. For a full commit SHA in a shell command, use `git rev-list -1 HEAD`.
- The hook also blocks these reads in subagents. To give a subagent a diff, write it to a file with `git diff <base>...HEAD -- . > <file>`, and give it the path.
- For a plain GET or HEAD, use `http-fetch` or `http-head` under the same prefix.

## Edit files

- Three or more edits in one file: use `mcp__anvil-emacs-eval__file-batch`. Do not make separate calls for one logical edit.
- Otherwise use `file-replace-string`, `file-replace-regexp`, `file-insert-at-line`, `file-delete-lines`, or `file-append` under the same prefix. Built-in `Edit` is also allowed for small changes.
- Avoid repeated full-file reads and repeated elisp patterns. When you see one of these patterns during a task, change to a targeted tool immediately.
- Never use Anvil org MCP tools. Edit org files with Read and Edit. The reason is in [shell.md](~/.claude/agent-rules/shell.md).
- Run heavy Emacs operations with `mcp__anvil__emacs-eval-async`, and poll with `emacs-eval-jobs` and `emacs-eval-result`. For worker pools, scheduled tasks, and large output, use the `anvil-advanced-ops` skill.

## Route work

- Web research or reading a web page: read [web.md](~/.claude/agent-rules/web.md) first.
- Private or historical questions: search local archives first. For current-state questions, also check that the facts are current.
- When a subagent or delegated worker reports back, check its evidence before you accept it.
- In Claude Code, run each parallel or lasting job as a separate harness task with `run_in_background: true`, one task for each target. Never detach lasting work with `&`. Run quick commands in the foreground.

# Web research

- Search with `kagi_search_fetch`.
- Read a page with `http-fetch` (under `mcp__anvil-emacs-eval__`) and `selector="p"`. A `selector` that matches nothing returns the whole page body, so check `extract-miss` in the result.
- For a page in Chinese or another non-ASCII language, start with `kagi_extract`: it returns clean markdown in one call, and `http-fetch` returns such text as octal-escaped bytes.
- For a page that needs JavaScript or gives an empty result, use `kagi_extract` or `browser-fetch`.
- Screenshot or live-UI bugs: use `$browser-use`.
